podcast.body: One of Pearl Jam's biggest songs from their *Ten* album, "Jeremy" intricately weaves together two distinct school shooting stories. The first involves a troubled seventh grader named Brian from Eddie Vedder's junior high in San Diego, who brought a sawed-off shotgun to school in the 1970s and shot up a fish tank, an event that deeply affected Vedder. The second, more central narrative, details the life and tragic suicide of 15-year-old Jeremy Dell of Richardson, Texas, who, after a history of psychiatric issues, suicidal attempts, and school disciplinary problems, ultimately shot himself in front of his English class on January 8, 1991. The song was inspired after Eddie Vedder read a newspaper story about Jeremy Dell. "It tells two stories that are intertwined into one and both involve school shootings."

podcast.body: The first Jeremy video was financed personally by photographer Chris Cafaro (a friend of Eddie's), who took out a loan and sold half his guitar collection to fund it; Epic initially had no interest in Jeremy as a single. Filmed in a warehouse in Los Angeles on October 4, 1991, this version has a subtler, less graphic treatment. Epic later commissioned the well-known Mark Pellington video in June 1992, which won multiple awards but featured graphic blood spatters and a suicide scene eventually censored. The experience soured Pearl Jam on making videos; they didn't release another until 1998 (*Do the Evolution* from *Yield*). The song was inspired by Jeremy Dell, a student who shot himself with a .357 Magnum in front of his English class in Richardson, Texas, on January 8, 1991. In 1996, the shooter in the Moses Lake, Washington school shootings (three killed) cited the Pellington video as an influence. "Epic Pearl Jam's record label, was not keen on the idea. They didn't think Jeremy had any potential whatsoever as a single."

podcast.body: The song tells the story of Jeremy Wade Dell, a 16-year-old from Richardson, Texas, who committed suicide in front of his English class on January 8, 1991. Jeremy, a loner with divorced parents, pulled out a loaded .357 magnum and shot himself in the mouth after his teacher, Fay Berrett, admonished him for missing classes. The incident received international attention, occurring seven years before the Columbine tragedy, highlighting the then-unfathomable idea of a student bringing a gun to school to kill himself. Eddie Vedder was particularly affected by this story because of a similar incident from his own school days in San Diego, where a classmate named Brian brought a sawed-off shotgun to school and shot up a fish tank. Vedder, who had previously had a confrontation with Brian, wondered if he had been in the wrong place at the wrong time and feared more serious consequences could have occurred. "One guy who was particularly fascinated was this surfer dude from San Diego named Eddie Vetter."

podcast.body: This song became a major hit for Pearl Jam and was inspired by the true story of 16-year-old Jeremy Wade Dell, who committed suicide in front of his English class on January 8, 1991, in Richardson, Texas. Eddie Vedder was fascinated by the story, partly due to a personal experience in school where a classmate shot a fish tank with a sawed-off shotgun. Jeremy Dell's father, Joseph Dell, later expressed deep anguish over the song's popularity and the resulting attention from fans who visited his son's grave, left notes, and created websites, often idealizing Jeremy's actions and expressing adoration for Eddie Vedder. "My anguish is just as deep with each call, note or email."

The video became an MTV sensation and notably swept the MTV Video Music Awards the year following its release. "Jeremy, whose harrowing cinematic video depicting an abused child taunted at school, became an MTV sensation."
